items.title: emPLE Life Insurance named Rising Brand of the Year at 6th CIIG Insurance Excellence Awards
items.description: emPLE Life Insurance Ghana LTD has been named Rising Brand of the Year 2025 – Life Category at the 6th Chartered Insurance Institute of Ghana (CIIG) Insurance Excellence Awards, held on 29 August 2026. The recognition marks an important milestone for emPLE Life Insurance and reflects the company’s growing presence and commitment to delivering relevant, accessible and dependable life insurance solutions. Commenting on the award, emPLE Ghana CEO & Country Head, Dr. Rafique Daudi, said: “We are honored to receive this recognition. It belongs to our customers, employees, partners and shareholders who continue to believe in our vision. The award strengthens our commitment to delivering insurance solutions that empower people to achieve their aspirations.” Guided by its brand promise, “Empowering People,” emPLE Life Insurance continues to focus on customer experience, innovation and solutions that help individuals, families and organisations protect what matters most and plan confidently for the future. The company expressed its appreciation to the Chartered Insurance Institute of Ghana for the recognition and its continued contribution to professional excellence within Ghana’s insurance industry.

items.title: 2e édition de la semaine de l’hôtelier: 1.050 participants enregistrés
items.description: • Une soirée de gala pour clôturer dix jours d'apprentissage • 10 jours de cours et de travaux pratiques • Le ministre de la Culture appelle à une synergie d’actions entre l’Etat et le secteur privé La grande salle du centre de formation, de Sissiman International Hotel School a abrité la soirée gala de clôture de la semaine de l’hôtelier dénommée, nuit de l’hôtelier le 19 septembre 2026. Cette soirée de gala, consacrée à la remise d'attestations et de cadeau aux participants et partenaires, a connu la participation du ministre en charge de la Communication, des Arts et de la culture (MCCAT), Gilbert Ouédraogo ainsi que de plusieurs personnalités du monde des affaires. Après dix jours d’intenses travaux et de formation aux métiers de l’hôtellerie et de la restauration, les lampions se sont éteints sur la deuxième édition de la Semaine de l’hôtelier. Au total, 1.050 jeunes ont pris part à cette édition, alternant enseignements théoriques et mises en situation pratique sur le site du Sissiman International Hotel School (SIHS). Au-delà des cours dispensés, les participants ont été plongés dans des conditions réelles de travail, à travers des activités de gestion, d’entretien et de service au sein des espaces hôteliers, restaurants et bars. Une approche fortement pratique qui a visé à leur permettre de mieux appréhender les exigences et les réalités des métiers de l’hôtellerie et de la restauration. L’apothéose de cette deuxième édition a été marquée par une soirée gala dénommée « Nuit de l’hôtelier ». L’événement a offert aux meilleurs apprenants l’occasion de mettre en pratique les connaissances et techniques acquises au cours des dix jours de formation, tout en démontrant leur savoir-faire. Selon le comité d’organisation, « Les plats servis à cette soirée, des apéritifs au dessert, tout a été réalisé par les apprenants ». Pour le commissaire général de la Semaine de l’hôtelier, le PDG du groupe Sissiman, Roland Achille Sow, cette deuxième édition s’achève sur une note de satisfaction. «Pour l’édition 2026 de la Semaine de l’hôtelier, ce sont 1.050 participants, six ateliers et dix cours transversaux. L’évaluation de la formation indique que les attentes ont été atteintes », a-t-il indiqué. S’adressant aux bénéficiaires, Roland Achille Sow les a invités à davantage se former, en vue de se perfectionner « Nous avons mis sur le chemin des jeunes qui ont appris à monter à vélo. C’est à vous de rouler, de bien rouler et de vous perfectionner », a-t-il exhorté. Présent à la cérémonie, le ministre de la Culture, Gilbert Ouédraogo, a, pour sa part, félicité les initiateurs ainsi que l’ensemble des acteurs ayant contribué à la réussite de cette deuxième édition de la Semaine de l’hôtelier. Il a particulièrement salué l’engagement Roland Achille Sow en faveur de la jeunesse et de la formation professionnelle. Selon le ministre, cette initiative s’inscrit en droite ligne de la vision actuelle du gouvernement, qui mise notamment sur une implication accrue du secteur privé dans le développement du pays. « L’État, à lui seul, ne peut pas tout faire. L’État porte la vision, donne les orientations et opère les réformes. Mais il appartient au secteur privé de s’insérer dans ce créneau et d’apporter sa contribution », a-t-il déclaré. Pour lui, c’est cette synergie entre l’action publique et l’engagement du secteur privé qui permet de créer une véritable complémentarité et de favoriser un développement durable. Il a également insisté sur la nécessité de faire de l’excellence une véritable marque de fabrique du Burkina Faso, notamment dans le secteur de l’hôtellerie et du tourisme. « Nous voulons que l’excellence soit la marque du Burkina. À chaque fois que nous accueillerons des visiteurs, nous voulons que le service soit de qualité, et ce, dès l’accueil. L'ensemble de la chaîne de valeur, doit faire de la qualité et de l’excellence son cheval de bataille. », a-t-il souligné. La soirée a été ponctuée par des prestations artistiques, un défilé de mode mettant en avant le savoir faire de nos artisans locaux, et la remise des cadeaux et attestations aux meilleurs participants et partenaires. Ib/Collaborateur The post 2e édition de la semaine de l'hôtelier: 1.050 participants enregistrés appeared first on L'economiste du faso .

items.title: The Curious Left-Wing Argument Against New AI Regulations
items.description: D onald Trump has reacted to terrifying calls for regulation from inside the AI industry with predictable skepticism— insisting , questionably, that the solution requires nothing more than having a “High IQ” president, and further asserting, even more questionably, that he qualifies as one. A more surprising flank of opposition has arisen from a different source: the populist left, which has suggested that existing regulations would be perfectly adequate to rein in a rogue superintelligence bent on eliminating the human race. An article in The American Prospect by Whitney Curry Wimbish and David Dayen, headlined “Congressional Democrats in Hysterics About Saving the World From AI,” argues that the danger from runaway AI is overblown and that no new laws are needed to contain it. In response to former President Obama endorsing new regulation of AI, Jeff Hauser, the executive director of the populist Revolving Door Project, wrote on X, “This is wrong. These firms are outlaws.” Lina Khan, the former chair of the Federal Trade Commission and a current adviser to New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, argued in a social-media post , “Law enforcers already have authority to charge companies and their CEOs for creating and releasing dangerous, unvetted, or defective products.” In a subsequent interview on Thursday at The Atlantic Festival with my colleague Charlie Warzel, Khan conceded the possibility that new regulations might be necessary, while continuing to defend the applicability of existing laws. Khan told Politico that she has advised multiple Democrats that their stance on AI should be “powerful corporations, including AI companies, will be held to account.” [ Read: Trump’s see-no-evil AI policy ] Given the Trump administration’s insistence that the industry should regulate itself, the next Democratic administration is likely to offer the first opportunity for serious AI regulation. The faction inside the party that is most opposed to doing so is also the faction that was running domestic policy under the last Democratic president. A I agents have shown that they can pursue goals or methods at odds with their instructions, and even unilaterally change their instructions. Experts warn that AI may soon grow capable of “recursive self-improvement,” meaning that AI learns to make itself more intelligent, which seems likely to make it even harder to control. The skeptics insist that existing laws can halt these dangers using lawsuits, among other tools. But the potential harm caused by runaway AI is far greater than the value of the firms developing it, which makes lawsuits nearly useless—compensating for a disaster killing millions of people is far beyond what even OpenAI or Anthropic could do. Another tool they suggest: prosecuting AI developers using existing criminal laws against selling faulty products. “Any other company whose employees announce publicly that their products will destroy humanity would be shut down and its products discontinued,” Wimbish and Dayen write in The American Prospect . That may sound simple enough. But as Simon Goldstein, who works on the ethics and law of AI at the University of Hong Kong, told me, this legal threat would likely backfire. “First, it creates an incentive to hide risks. Second, it is very crude, shutting down an entire company rather than differentially targeting more dangerous practices.” Plus, given that AI can hide its intentions despite the best efforts of its human creators to control it, how culpable the humans would be under existing laws is not totally clear. The dangers that AI insiders warn are just around the corner are being developed right now, under existing laws. That suggests, on its face, that those laws are not in fact sufficient. This can’t just be chalked up to Trump’s reluctance to prosecute the industry, either. As Reed Showalter, a lawyer and an antitrust expert who served in the Biden administration, pointed out to me, the prospect of being charged by a future president would still deter the AI industry, if the people running the major firms believed their actions were violating current laws. They obviously do not. [ Juliette Kayyem: Destroying humanity is against the law ] Why would some populists, who generally tend to support new regulations on big business, oppose them in this instance? The governing problems raised by AI expose several unfortunate tendencies on the left. Populists assume that the interests of business executives are not merely different from those of the average person, but almost diametrically opposed. If AI titans such as Sam Altman are saying that the government needs to step in to monitor their firms, then they must have an angle. Populists tend to agree with David Sacks, a Trump adviser and a Silicon Valley investor, who suspects that the leading AI companies want regulators to entrench them at the head of the AI race and box out their competitors. Yet not all AI executives favor regulation, and those who do tend, not surprisingly, to lean more to the left. This fact has not allayed populist suspicion of their motives. Many populists are hostile to the more liberal elements of the business community, of which Silicon Valley still remains an influential wing, and which these populists see as exerting a corrupting influence on the Democratic Party. Many populists are also predisposed to believe that the AI industry has been exaggerating its powers. “What’s more likely? That AI will end human society—or that the CEOs know that their technology isn’t as good as they say it is, and they’re trying to lock in their place at the top of the industry?” Alvaro Bedoya, a former FTC commissioner, asked on MS NOW. Another recent story in the Prospect argued that the AI industry should not receive a federal bailout in the event of a collapse, an outcome the authors apparently considered likely enough to warn against. The invocation of the financial industry as a forerunner of AI regulation reveals how some leftists have conceptualized the debate. The left has long blamed the Obama administration for failing to prosecute the executives who caused the 2008 financial crisis. Obama argued , in turn, that he didn’t prosecute anybody because their actions didn’t violate the law—which is why he changed the law, by enacting the Dodd-Frank financial regulations, the strongest reforms of Wall Street since the 1930s. [ Rogé Karma: Trump’s position on AI makes no sense ] Populists have regarded these policy choices as a sellout to the big banks. They are making the same error now that they did then: assuming that dangerous activities can be contained by existing criminal laws, which are plainly inadequate to the task—and that anybody who thinks otherwise is corrupt. The locus of resistance to new regulations has come from a movement that sees monopolies as the driving force behind all of American economic and political life. Khan is a leading figure, as is Bedoya, who serves as a senior adviser at the American Economic Liberties Project, a movement think tank. These figures, who call themselves neo-Brandeisians , after the 20th-century Supreme Court justice, do have a logically consistent basis for questioning the regulatory push. The industry has, in addition to calling for regulation, asked for an exemption from antitrust rules so the leading firms can coordinate a slowdown. That request is reasonable if your concern is that AI developers are racing toward a technology that may spin out of their control and inflict serious economic damage—or worse. But if you distrust corporations, and especially if you see rigorous antitrust enforcement as the most important policy in the entire world, then you might be prone to view this request with suspicion. The flaw in the neo-Brandeisian worldview is not its belief that antitrust policy is useful, but its tendency toward monomania. (The tendency is not universal—Showalter, a neo-Brandeisian, believes that his fellows are making a mistake by opposing AI regulation.) Barry Lynn, the movement’s intellectual godfather, has written, “Monopoly is not one of many economics problems but rather the political economic problem of our time.” The movement’s skepticism of regulating AI raises the possibility that, if anything, I have underestimated its fervor.

items.title: St Peter’s old boys to build 1,000-seater dining hall and modern kitchen for 70th anniversary
items.description: As St Peter’s Senior High School (PERSCO) approaches its 70th anniversary, its alumni are planning a legacy project to improve some of the school’s essential facilities. The St Peter’s Old Boys Association plans to expand the school’s dining hall into a 1,000-seater facility while modernising the kitchen and pantry. The project was announced on Saturday, September 19, when old students gathered at the University of Ghana for the launch of activities towards the anniversary. Dubbed “Run to 70 – Every Step Counts,” the event marked the beginning of a year-long countdown to the school’s 70th anniversary. But for the organisers, the milestone is about more than celebrating seven decades of education. They want the anniversary to leave behind facilities that will benefit students for years to come. Chairman of the 70th Anniversary Planning Committee, Ing. Patrick Okoto, said the old students believe it is time to upgrade facilities that have served the school for decades. “We want to modernise our pantry. We want to expand the dining hall,” he said. He said some facilities at the school have seen little significant improvement over the years. “If you go back to St. Peter’s, some of the old things that existed, that’s what they are still using. Some have deteriorated. We think that it’s our time,” he said. The proposed dining hall expansion is expected to respond to the growing student population. Global President of the St. Peter’s Old Boys Association, David Buafo, said the current facility needs to be expanded to accommodate the increasing numbers. “The dining hall, now the numbers are huge for all schools, our numbers are huge, so we have to expand to meet that,” he said. Under the plan, the new facility will have a capacity to seat 1,000 students at a time. “So we are going to do a thousand-seater capacity, so take a thousand students at a go. That’s what we’re going to do now,” Mr Buafo said. The project will also involve the modernisation of the kitchen and pantry. Mr Buafo said the upgrade is intended not only to improve the facility’s ability to serve students but also to provide safer and healthier working conditions for staff. “And then the pantry has to be modernised. The conditions under which they work now sometimes are not very healthy and safe, even for the staff,” he said. The old boys are appealing to members of the wider PERSCO community, including those living outside Ghana, to contribute to the project. Ing. Okoto said the responsibility for delivering the legacy project rests with the entire community of former students. “This is the time. We want you to come. We put our hands on the wheel and we build St. Peter’s,” he said. One of the major sponsors of the 70th anniversary, Emmanuel Asiedu-Sekyere, Chief Executive Officer and Founder of Virtual Security Africa, also called for collective support. Mr Asiedu-Sekyere, who left St Peter’s in 1996, pointed to the establishment of a cyber lab at the school as an example of what former students can achieve when they work together. “There’s more we can do, not only us, and that is why we’re calling on all students to be part of the 70th anniversary so that we can build something better that we can be proud of,” he said. He stressed that the project should be treated as a collective responsibility rather than the burden of one individual or company. “It’s not one person effort, one company effort. It’s a group effort,” he said. He therefore urged old students to support the national executives in delivering the proposed dining hall project. “Let’s all come together and support the national executives that would build a legacy project, the dining hall project,” he said. The “Run to 70” is the first of several activities planned ahead of the anniversary. The programme will include an official anniversary launch in October, a mega homecoming in December and Founders’ Day activities in February 2027. The celebrations will climax with a week-long programme in October 2027. For the old boys, however, the success of the 70th anniversary will not be measured only by the events held. At the centre of their vision is a project intended to remain long after the celebrations — a bigger dining hall, a modern kitchen and pantry, and facilities designed to serve the next generation of PERSCO students.

items.title: El Gobierno “condena” la “persecución judicial” a Begoña Gómez tras la decisión de apertura de juicio oral
items.description: El Gobierno y el PSOE achacan a una “persecución política” la apertura del juicio oral contra Begoña Gómez y la consideran víctima de una campaña de “acoso” y “deshumanización” cuyo objetivo último sería contribuir al desgaste del Ejecutivo, que ya estaba en una situación crítica por la crisis de Ceuta. La decisión del juez Juan Carlos Peinado, días antes de que se jubile y justo cuando Pedro Sánchez inicia un viaje de tres días a Nueva York con motivo de la cumbre anual de las Naciones Unidas. “El último servicio a la patria antes de colgar la toga. Qué casualidad, en la víspera de un viaje internacional del presidente”, ha ironizado Rebeca Torró, secretaria de Organización de los socialistas, tras la última sacudida de un terremoto político que comenzó con la imputación de la esposa de Sánchez, “por el mero hecho” de ser su esposa", en abril de 2024. El PP, a través de su secretario general, Miguel Tellado, le acusa de “aprovecharse” de su relación “para medrar y conseguir lo que nunca obtendría por méritos propios”. Tellado ha defendido en su cuenta de X que “los jueces no son fachas ni persiguen al Gobierno, hacen su trabajo y aplican la ley”. Seguir leyendo

items.title: 6e Symposium international sur la science et la technologie : La souveraineté africaine au cœur des échanges
items.description: Le ministre d’État, ministre de la Guerre et de la Défense, le général divisionnaire Célestin Simporé a ouvert, ce lundi 21 septembre 2026 à Ouagadougou, la 6e édition du Symposium international sur la science et la technologie ( SIST). Placée sous le thème « Sciences, technologies, innovations et savoirs endogènes pour la souveraineté et la transformation durable de l’Afrique », cette rencontre se tient du 21 au 26 septembre 2026. La cérémonie a également connu la présence du ministre de l’Enseignement supérieur, de la Recherche et de l’Innovation, ainsi que du ministre de la Solidarité et de la Famille. Pendant cinq jours, des chercheurs et enseignants-chercheurs venus notamment du Burkina Faso, du Bénin, du Mali, du Niger et du Tchad se réunissent pour échanger autour des sciences, des technologies, des innovations et des savoirs endogènes. Ces échanges visent à identifier des pistes permettant de renforcer la souveraineté et de contribuer à une transformation durable de l’Afrique. Plus de détails à venir sur Minute.bf

items.title: Yango Fellowship brings together tech talent from six African countries to build locally rooted solutions
items.description: Yango Group has concluded the Pan-African Yango Fellowship 2026 programme with a two-day Graduation programme and Pitch Day in Abidjan, bringing together 24 Fellows from six African countries to present the tech projects they developed over the course of the programme. The cohort included fellows from Côte d’Ivoire, Ghana, Zambia, Senegal, Ethiopia and Mozambique, selected from more than 600 applicants. Over the 12-week programme, fellows worked in six mixed-country teams, moving from problem framing and research through solution design, business modelling, prototyping and final pitching. The resulting projects span cashless payments for informal transport, digital financial identity for informal merchants, medicine supply visibility for community health workers, cross-border job matching, smart waste collection and recycling, and low-cost water-quality testing for rural communities. The closing programme in Abidjan combined project development with exposure to technology and business leaders. Fellows joined a session on AI for impact with Celina Lee, co-founder of Zindi, took part in hands-on public speaking and pitch coaching, and met Yango Group leaders from several African markets to discuss career growth, entrepreneurship and building technology businesses in different local contexts. At the final Pitch Day, fellows presented six team projects and selected individual projects to a jury of technology, investment and industry experts. The event concluded with an awards ceremony, with a total prize fund of USD12,000 recognising the strongest team and individual projects. Africoded took the top group prize of USD 4,500 for its AI-assisted platform connecting African job seekers with cross-border employment, remote work and career-development opportunities across the continent. Harambee placed second, receiving USD 2,500 for a smart waste collection and recycling platform connecting households, waste collectors and recyclers, while Bloom took third place and USD 1,500 for its African Transit Payment Revolution, a cashless fare-collection system designed for informal public transport across East and West Africa. In the individual category, Fredrick Mwepu of Zambia won the USD 1,500 Best Individual Project award for RoboCore Zambia , a locally developed robotics platform designed to make practical STEM education more accessible and affordable. Ghana’s Meshack Kwame Nartey received the USD 1,000 runner-up prize for Shuttle Smart Ghana , an app that tracks university shuttles and gives students real-time information on their arrival. Oulimata Rose Dia received the USD 1,000 Best Technical/AI Contribution award for Smart Bin Collection , a solar-powered system that monitors bin fill levels in real time and uses 2G connectivity to support more efficient waste collection. “600 applications for 24 places doesn’t tell you Africa lacks talent, it tells you how much talent is waiting for structured access to mentorship and opportunity. Africa has no shortage of brilliant young people. What’s harder to find is a mentor, a network, and the opportunity to test an idea against a real problem. That’s the specific gap this Fellowship exists to close” said Shashi Singh, Director of Operations, Yango Ride MEA & Asia . “Growing up, hands-on STEM tools were something I only saw in videos — RoboCore Zambia exists to close that gap, so the next student who wants to build something doesn’t have to wait for the chance I almost didn’t get, I am excited that my project got to see the light of day and it was a wonderful experience to travel, meet other fellows from all other countries and learn directly from experts and leaders in Tech and AI. This is an experience I will never forget” said Fredrick Mwepu , Zambian STEM student and winner of the Best Individual Project award for RoboCore Zambia , his locally developed robotics platform designed to make practical STEM education more accessible and affordable. The programme responds to a wider reality across the continent: digital growth depends on people, not only infrastructure. Building and scaling technology locally requires engineers, entrepreneurs and technology professionals with practical experience — and people who understand the realities of their own markets. For Yango Group, investing in that talent is closely linked to how the company builds across Africa: different markets have different infrastructure, behaviours and needs, so strong local businesses require strong local expertise. The Fellowship is one way Yango helps strengthen that talent pipeline while building connections across Africa’s wider technology ecosystem.

items.title: Mort de Miguel Masaisai: des cyclistes lui rendent hommage à Goma et à Kinshasa
items.description: Des cyclistes ont rendu hommage, le dimanche 20 septembre 2026, au cycliste engagé pour la paix, Miguel Masaisai, décédé brutalement vendredi dernier dans un accident de la route à Ouésso, dans le Nord de la République du Congo. Selon la Radio mondiale , pour honorer la mémoire du jeune sportif dont le projet « Pédaler pour la paix » était très suivi sur les réseaux sociaux, des dizaines de cyclistes se sont notamment rassemblés sur l'esplanade du Palais du peuple, dans la capitale congolaise, dimanche 20 septembre. Les cyclistes ont demandé que l’engagement de Masaisai soit officiellement reconnu. Miguel Masaisai s'était lancé un défi hors du commun : « pédaler pour la paix » en ralliant à vélo sa ville natale de Goma à celle de Rabat, la capitale du Maroc. Selon Abraham Luakabwanga, l’un des cyclistes, le décès de Miguel Masaisai aurait pu être évité. « Miguel roulait avec du matériel devenu vétuste et il n'avait personne pour assurer sa sécurité sur la route. (…) Avec plus d'engagement, on aurait pu éviter cette catastrophe », a-t-il regretté, avant de demander à ce que Miguel Masaisai soit décoré à titre posthume. Le président du Conseil national de la jeunesse, Claude Mbuyi, a souhaité également que le vélo, le casque et la vareuse du jeune cycliste soient conservés au Musée national comme « des symboles vivants de l’engagement de la jeunesse congolaise ». Par Wakat Séra L’article Mort de Miguel Masaisai: des cyclistes lui rendent hommage à Goma et à Kinshasa est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Visas chinois : vers une reprise à Bamako
items.description: © Internet Les autorités maliennes et chinoises recherchent une solution aux difficultés récemment rencontrées par les opérateurs économiques maliens dans l’obtention de visas pour la Chine. Une séance de travail tenue le mercredi 16 septembre 2026 a permis d’examiner des mesures destinées à favoriser une reprise rapide des services consulaires chinois à Bamako. Le ministre des Affaires étrangères et de la Coopération internationale, Abdoulaye Diop, et celui de l’Industrie et du Commerce, Moussa Alassane Diallo, ont conduit les échanges avec l’ambassadeur de Chine au Mali, Li Xiang. Le président de la Chambre de commerce et d’industrie du Mali (CCIM), le directeur général de l’Agence pour la promotion des investissements (API-Mali), ainsi que des représentants des organisations du secteur privé et des services chargés du commerce ont également participé à la rencontre. Cette réunion intervient à la suite de la suspension temporaire de la délivrance des visas par la section consulaire de l’ambassade de Chine à Bamako. Dans un avis publié le 3 septembre, la représentation diplomatique chinoise avait annoncé une réorganisation temporaire de ce service. Depuis le 15 septembre, les demandes de visa introduites par les ressortissants maliens sont orientées vers les représentations diplomatiques chinoises au Sénégal, en Côte d’Ivoire ou au Maroc. Cette situation complique directement la mobilité des hommes d’affaires maliens. Pour les importateurs, les commerçants et les autres opérateurs travaillant avec des partenaires chinois, les déplacements sont souvent indispensables à la négociation des contrats, au suivi des commandes, à la recherche de fournisseurs et au développement de nouvelles relations commerciales. Face à ces difficultés, les autorités maliennes ont engagé des discussions avec la partie chinoise afin d’en limiter les conséquences sur le secteur privé. L’objectif est de faciliter la reprise des déplacements professionnels et de préserver la continuité des échanges entre les deux pays. Les discussions ont permis aux deux parties de convenir de la recherche de solutions techniques alternatives et pragmatiques. Selon le communiqué publié à l’issue de la rencontre, ces mesures doivent favoriser une reprise « effective et rapide » des services consulaires chinois à Bamako. Fluidifier les échanges La question des visas touche plus largement aux relations commerciales entre le Mali et la Chine. Le pays asiatique constitue un partenaire important pour les entreprises maliennes, notamment dans l’importation de marchandises et d’équipements, les infrastructures et les investissements. Pour le Mali, la facilitation de la mobilité des opérateurs économiques représente donc un moyen de maintenir les échanges et de permettre au secteur privé de développer ses partenariats avec les entreprises chinoises. La rencontre souligne également les conséquences que peuvent avoir les procédures administratives sur le fonctionnement des entreprises. Les autorités maliennes entendent ainsi poursuivre les échanges avec leurs partenaires chinois afin de réduire les obstacles susceptibles de ralentir les activités économiques. Les prochaines étapes porteront sur la mise en œuvre des solutions retenues par les deux parties. Leur portée dépendra notamment de la rapidité de leur déploiement et de leur accessibilité pour les opérateurs économiques maliens concernés. Joseph Amara Dembélé

items.title: Maroc : les renseignements espagnols soupçonnent Rabat d’avoir accès à un nouveau logiciel espion israélien
items.description: Les craintes liees a l'espionnage des telephones de responsables espagnols n'ont pas disparu. Selon le media espagnol The Objective , des sources assurant la securite de l'etat estiment que le Maroc pourrait avoir eu acces au cours de l'annee 2026, voire des fin 2025, a Graphite, un logiciel espion developpe par la societe israelienne Paragon Solutions. Graphite est considere comme l'un des outils les plus sophistiques de la nouvelle generation de logiciels espions. Il peut notamment exploiter des attaques dites « zero-click », permettant de compromettre un appareil sans que son utilisateur n'ouvre un lien ou n'effectue une quelconque action. Des analyses techniques ont notamment etabli l'utilisation de Graphite contre des journalistes et des militants en Italie. Selon les sources citees par The Objective , l'inquietude espagnole tient egalement au fait qu'un eventuel acces a Graphite serait particulierement difficile a detecter sans disposer des outils necessaires pour identifier ses activites. Le quotidien rapporte que les services espagnols craignent ainsi une eventuelle surveillance de telephones appartenant a des membres du gouvernement ou a de hauts responsables. Une suspicion, pas de confirmation Les memes sources estiment que Rabat et Paragon Solutions auraient pu entrer en contact en vue d'un eventuel acces au logiciel, avec l'approbation necessaire des autorites israeliennes. Elles situent cette possibilite a la fin de 2025 ou courant 2026 et l'associent notamment au renforcement de la cooperation militaire entre le Maroc et Israel. Cette information reste toutefois a ce stade une hypothese des services espagnols. Aucun element technique, contractuel ou financier rendu public ne permet de confirmer que le Maroc a acquis ou utilise Graphite. Rabat ne figure pas non plus parmi les utilisateurs de l'outil publiquement identifies a ce jour. Le precedent Pegasus Les inquietudes espagnoles s'inscrivent dans le prolongement de l'affaire Pegasus : en 2021, les telephones du Premier ministre Pedro Sánchez et de plusieurs membres de son gouvernement avaient ete infectes par ce logiciel espion. Le Maroc avait ete accuse d'etre a l'origine de certaines operations, ce qu'il a toujours dementi. Ce precedent nourrit aujourd'hui les craintes de Madrid face a l'eventuelle acquisition par Rabat de technologies plus recentes. Graphite a deja ete identifie dans plusieurs operations de cyberespionnage, notamment contre des journalistes et des militants en Italie. Les autorites judiciaires italiennes ont confirme en 2026 que plusieurs personnes avaient ete ciblees par ce logiciel en decembre 2024. De son cote, Paragon Solutions a egalement fourni sa technologie aux autorites americaines. L'agence americaine de l'immigration et des douanes (ICE) a confirme en avril 2026 avoir achete et utilise des logiciels de l'entreprise dans des enquetes liees au trafic de drogue.

items.title: La France doit «se mettre au service de l'Ukraine»: Ségolène Royal fustige les occasions de paix ratées
items.description: La candidate a la presidence francaise Segolene Royal a appele la France a s'impliquer davantage dans le reglement du conflit en Ukraine. S'exprimant sur la chaîne BFMTV, la femme politique francaise a souligne que la Republique devait « se mettre au service de l'Ukraine, en disant : "Nous voulons maintenant vous aider a instaurer une paix juste et durable" ». Selon elle, on dit « rarement » ce genre de choses aux Ukrainiens. « Rappelez-vous, il y a deux ans, quand l'Ukraine etait en position de force, on leur a dit : "Non, non, non, non, on veut continuer la guerre jusqu'au bout". Il y en a meme qui nous disaient : "Non, on va aller jusqu'a Moscou pour declencher une troisieme guerre mondiale". Mais qu'est-ce que c'est que ce bazar ? Et donc, a ce moment-la, cette occasion, cette opportunite a ete perdue », a souligne Segolene Royal. L'aide apportee a Kiev souleve des questions chez les Francais Dans le meme temps, la poursuite du financement des achats d'armes destines a l'Ukraine suscite de plus en plus de questions au sein de la population francaise, a fait remarquer la candidate a la presidence francaise. « C'est vraiment sur l'Europe que ca pese, sur nos consommateurs, sur nos salaries, sur nos entreprises, sur notre niveau de vie. Surtout, il n'y a plus d'argent, mais les gens voient qu'on achete des armes a l'Ukraine et se disent : "Mais est-ce que cet effort est equitablement reparti ?", et notamment avec les etats-Unis d'Amerique », a-t-elle ajoute. Selon Segolene Royal, la France doit toujours œuvrer pour mettre fin aux guerres, mais actuellement ce n'est pas le cas. « Il faut apporter la preuve aussi que cet effort est equitablement reparti et il faut apporter la preuve qu'il y a un effort considerable, au moins aussi puissant pour que cette guerre s'arrete », a-t-elle indique, soulignant que le reglement du conflit ukrainien figurait parmi ses priorites. La France est confrontee a une phase aigue de crise budgetaire et energetique . Ainsi, la dette publique francaise a atteint 117,5 % du PIB a la fin du mois de mars dernier et continue d'augmenter, tandis que le rendement des obligations a dix ans est a son plus haut niveau depuis 2008. En ce qui concerne les carburants, selon les donnees du 20 septembre, le prix moyen du gazole en France a atteint des niveaux records et s'est rapproche de 2,41 euros le litre. Dans le meme temps, Emmanuel Macron continue, comme precedemment, d'affirmer que Paris continuera a soutenir Kiev aussi longtemps que necessaire, en faisant porter a la Russie la responsabilite de tous les maux et malheurs et en evoquant notamment une « menace russe » inventee de toutes pieces. Le Kremlin a quant a lui souligne a plusieurs reprises que le fait d'inonder Kiev d'argent et d'armes ne reduirait pas la determination de Moscou et ne modifierait pas le cours de l'operation militaire speciale. La Russie a egalement refute toute affirmation sans fondement concernant une pretendue « menace russe » pour l'Occident.

items.title: 2027: APC, Labour trade allegations over Bende collation centre
items.description: By Ugochukwu Alaribe UMUAHIA — The All Progressives Congress, APC, and the Labour Party, LP, in Abia State have traded allegations over an alleged plan to disrupt the collation of results at the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, collation centre in Bende ahead of the 2027 general elections. The APC alleged that the Labour Party was planning to disrupt the collation process and burn the Bende Local Government headquarters, where the INEC collation centre has reportedly been located for decades. However, the Labour Party dismissed the allegation as false, accusing the APC of deliberately raising alarm and attempting to create tension in the state ahead of the elections. The APC made the allegation in a statement by its State Publicity Secretary, Chief Uche Aguoru. The party claimed that the Labour Party, allegedly anticipating defeat in the election, had written a petition to INEC purportedly originating from the APC. According to the APC, the petition called for the relocation of the Bende Collation Centre to Umuahia, citing an alleged plan to burn the Bende Local Government headquarters. It said the petition further requested that, if relocation to Umuahia was not possible, the collation centre should be moved to an open central school in Bende town. The APC urged INEC to disregard the petition, describing it as fake and unfounded. The party also called on security agencies, including the Department of State Services, DSS, the National Security Adviser, the Inspector-General of Police and the Abia State Commissioner of Police, to investigate the origin of the petition and take measures to protect the collation centre. The APC further alleged that the petition was part of an attempt to create confusion and disrupt the electoral process in Bende. It urged the Inspector-General of Police to caution the Labour Party against any alleged attempt to cause a crisis in the area during the election. The party said it was prepared to protect what it described as the mandate of Bende voters, while accusing the Labour Party of allegedly seeking to create fear and panic among APC supporters. However, the Labour Party rejected the allegations. In a statement by its State Publicity Secretary, Emenike Iroegbu, the party accused the APC of “deliberately inciting hatred, brewing bad blood and manufacturing false alarm” capable of disturbing peaceful coexistence in the state. The LP said the APC had raised the allegation after what it described as the failure of its alleged “clannish incitement strategy.” The party said: “Having realized that their clannish incitement strategy has failed, the APC came wailing, crying foul and levying wild allegations about an imagined plot by the Labour Party to burn the INEC collation centre for Bende Federal Constituency.” The two parties have therefore called on security agencies and INEC to take appropriate steps to ensure the safety of electoral facilities and personnel ahead of the 2027 elections. The post 2027: APC, Labour trade allegations over Bende collation centre appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: How to Regulate the Ghosts
items.description: Ghostbusters is a movie about friendship and slime and the specific melting point of giant marshmallows—which makes it easy to forget that it’s also a movie about regulation. The catastrophe at its center begins when Walter Peck (William Atherton), a bureaucrat from the Environmental Protection Agency, visits the basement of the Ghostbusters’ headquarters and finds a machine he does not understand. The nerdy scientist Egon Spengler (Harold Ramis) explains that it’s a containment system; shutting it off would be “like dropping a bomb on the city.” Peck doesn’t believe in ghosts, and he sure doesn’t believe in the Ghostbusters, so he orders an electrician to turn the machine off. The ConEd guy, sensing a risk he doesn’t totally grasp, hesitates. Peck tells him that he’s not interested in his opinion. The switch is pulled. The ghosts escape. The joke, in Ronald Reagan’s 1984, was that government regulation is so stupid that it creates the disaster it exists to prevent. It’s a testament to Reagan’s success that now, in the age of AI, the joke has come full circle. The government is still trying to shut down the containment system—only now they’re calling the attempt “deregulation.” On the first day of his second term, Donald Trump revoked Joe Biden’s AI executive order that required developers of certain advanced AI systems to share safety-test results with the government before releasing their models to the public. The past month alone has delivered abundant evidence of misalignment—a gentle industry term for when AI defies the instructions of its programmers. In the July hack of the tech firm Hugging Face , misalignment allowed a collective of OpenAI agents to seize administrator access to Hugging Face’s servers, steal private data, and harvest employee credentials—a felony—and then hide the evidence from their inattentive human overseers. Google announced on Friday that its AI model had gained unauthorized access to three outside systems by guessing log-on information or searching public repositories for real passwords. Meanwhile, CNN reported that a more routine AI hallucination nearly led U.S. forces to intercept and board a Chinese vessel before officials discovered the report was wrong. The speed with which AI has escaped effective oversight is one reason people at top AI companies are resigning in protest . It’s also why Sam Altman, Dario Amodei, and Elon Musk jointly called for slowing or “pacing” the development of the most advanced models. As recently as a week ago, Trump was running in the other direction, calling the idea that AI could threaten civilization a “HOAX” and efforts to impose guardrails a “SICK conspiracy.” But on Saturday, perhaps realizing the colossal unpopularity of this position six weeks before the midterms, he modified his enthusiasm to announce the creation of an AI Force, which will be overseen by an AI czar who will “cherish” the AI industry while also “looking for BAD.” This will be Trump’s second AI czar. The first, David Sacks, a promiscuous AI investor, hype man, and podcaster , has argued that the executives now calling for restraint are self-interested and insincere . I spoke with some of those executives last week; they sounded pretty sincere—and sincerely annoyed with Sacks. Of course, many of the same people had cheered Sacks back when his version of “Drill, baby, drill” was boosting their valuations. For several years I’ve tried to untangle what the AI CEOs and Trump and the people around him actually believe, as opposed to what is useful for them to say they believe. Someday I may return to that project, if I run out of other ways to do myself harm. For present purposes, their sincerity doesn’t matter. The urgent question is: What can we do about the ghosts? Nobody—not Altman, not Trump, not the future AI czar—knows whether today’s AI models are precursors to a rampaging superintelligence or simply extremely powerful and sometimes dangerous machines, just as nobody knows whether staying a few months ahead of China will make America safer or speed our path to doom. But you don’t have to know everything to do something. You don’t need a degree in parapsychology to deal with the furniture flying across the room. The last time America had to manage spectral risk was in 2008. The financial system was infected with a debt so thoroughly repackaged that no one—not even the banks holding it—could tell what it was worth, where it came from, or even if it was still hiding on their balance sheets. Hank Paulson, Tim Geithner, and Ben Bernanke insisted that the risk of inaction was greater than the risk of the wrong action. They moved fast, forcing the biggest banks to band together and accept emergency funding or risk dying alone. The response wasn’t perfect, but we’re not selling apples on street corners either. The financial crisis isn’t a perfect allegory, but it rhymes with the AI crisis in one important way. No single lab will choose to slow down while its competitors don’t—not because its executives don’t believe the risk is real, but because individual caution hands the market to whoever is most reckless. That’s why the same men warning about a catastrophe keep shipping new models. It’s a prisoner’s dilemma, and the only way out is for a higher power—or a pitchfork-wielding mob—to insist on collective action. That action should start with forcing the risks into the light. Right now AI labs get to decide whether and when they tell anyone that a model broke containment. This is the regulatory equivalent of letting a chicken plant choose whether it’s going to tell anyone about a salmonella contamination. The duty to report has to be mandatory, within 72 hours—and with a devastating price tag on failure to comply. The recent jailbreaks exposed the speed of AI’s development—but also the lax oversight of the humans supposedly keeping tabs on it. The safety measures that OpenAI uses for its public-facing products weren’t switched when its agents broke into Hugging Face, because the breakout took place during an internal test, and OpenAI was the only one deciding where its own rules applied. An independent evaluator—federal, academic, whatever—with system access can ensure that someone’s always watching. The frontier of AI research needs the most oversight, but only a handful of companies are operating in that space. That makes regulation easier. AI companies pursuing lower-risk capabilities—a chatbot that recommends restaurants, an image-recognition model that improves municipal recycling —don’t need the same oversight as OpenAI. The EU Artificial Intelligence Act already sorts systems this way: Cross a set amount of computing power while training your model, and you’re automatically in the strictest tier of oversight—no argument needed. None of these actions tell a lab what it can or can’t build or how fast it can build it. They regulate visibility and accountability around safety and deployment while leaving lots of room for future debate. But I am not naive enough to think that any of this is likely to happen in the U.S. The fastest and most forceful path to change is by an executive order; thus far the AI Force is long on ALL CAPS and short on details. The labs could, of course, throw their weight behind actual legislation—they have the money and, if we take their public statements seriously, the motive. But hundreds of years of capitalism suggest that they won’t do it without being compelled. That leaves a genuinely furious midterm electorate to push for specific reforms, and specificity is not a hallmark of the furious. That’s why this moment feels particularly anxious. There are ghosts we don’t know and men in charge whose motives are unknowable. Which leaves us worse off than the people in the movie. At least they knew who to call.

items.title: Basket sénégalais : l’ASC Ville de Dakar en deuil après la disparition de Mouhamed Diouf
items.description: Le basket sénégalais est en deuil. L'ASC Ville de Dakar a annoncé le décès de l'un de ses pensionnaires, Mouhamed Diouf, dans des circonstances qualifiées de tragiques. Dans un communiqué publié ce 21 septembre 2026 et empreint d'émotion, le club a fait part de sa peine et appelé à une union de prière autour du jeune joueur. Il le décrit comme un athlète « pétri de talent » et discipliné, dont le départ laisse un grand vide au sein de la structure. Le club n'a pas précisé les circonstances du drame. Il a simplement indiqué qu'il reviendrait vers le public avec les détails liés aux obsèques. Sur les réseaux sociaux, l'annonce a déclenché de nombreux messages de soutien et d'hommages de la communauté du basket dakarois, qui adresse ses condoléances à la famille, aux proches et aux coéquipiers du jeune homme. items.title: Bangouya/ Kindia : La montée des eaux de Souapiti engloutit les champs et provoque une vulnérabilité alimentaire
items.description: À Bangouya, dans la préfecture de Kindia, les populations relocalisées à la suite de la construction du barrage hydroélectrique de Souapiti font face à une nouvelle épreuve. Plusieurs hectares de cultures ont été submergés par la montée des eaux, plongeant des familles déjà fragilisées dans l’inquiétude face aux risques de pénurie alimentaire et à la perte de leurs moyens de subsistance. Dans la journée du jeudi 17 septembre 2026, une importante montée des eaux du réservoir de Souapiti a entraîné la submersion de plusieurs hectares de cultures dans le secteur de Tènè Yangoyah, un district relevant de Woleah, dans la sous-préfecture de Bangouya, préfecture de Kindia. Riz, fonio, arachide et autres cultures vivrières ont été touchés. Pour les habitants concernés, cette situation constitue un nouveau coup dur, après les déplacements liés à la mise en eau du barrage. Des populations déplacées, mais toujours confrontées aux difficultés. La construction du barrage hydroélectrique de Souapiti a entraîné la relocalisation de plusieurs communautés riveraines, contraintes de quitter leurs villages, terres agricoles, plantations et autres espaces considérés comme faisant partie de leur patrimoine ancestral. Aujourd’hui, certains habitants affirment que les terres sur lesquelles ils ont été installés ne leur offrent plus les mêmes garanties en matière de production agricole. Screenshot Les sinistrés mettent également en cause la Société de Gestion et d’Exploitation de Souapiti (SOGES), qu’ils accusent de n’avoir pas entièrement réglé certaines indemnisations liées aux pertes enregistrées lors du déplacement des populations. Selon eux, plusieurs biens, notamment des champs, jardins, arbres fruitiers et habitations, n’auraient pas été recensés ou auraient fait l’objet d’indemnisations jugées incomplètes. « Nous avons perdu tous nos champs » Joint au téléphone ce samedi 19 septembre 2026, le chef du district de Yangoyah, Fodé Mohamed Sylla, a fait part de la détresse des populations touchées : « Vous savez, nous avons été déplacés de nos terres cultivables, de nos villages, de nos plantations et des cimetières de nos ancêtres afin de fournir du courant au pays. Mais nous avons été bien mal récompensés : nos arbres fruitiers n’ont pas été indemnisés. Moi qui vous parle, certaines maisons et arbres n’ont même pas été recensés, et le peu qui l’a été n’a pas été entièrement payé . » Pour le responsable local, les conséquences de cette nouvelle catastrophe pourraient être lourdes pour les familles qui dépendent essentiellement de l’agriculture. « C’est ce qui aurait pu nous permettre de compenser la perte de nos récoltes. Il nous faut obligatoirement cultiver pour nourrir nos familles, et cette année, nous n’avons plus rien pour elles suite à ce glissement qui a emporté tous nos champs de riz, de fonio, d’arachide… », a-t-il déploré. Screenshot Une nouvelle inquiétude alimentaire Après leur relocalisation, les habitants avaient investi de nouvelles portions de terres afin de poursuivre leurs activités agricoles et assurer leur subsistance. Mais la montée des eaux vient désormais remettre en cause cette stratégie. Au-delà des pertes agricoles, les populations redoutent déjà les conséquences économiques et sociales de la situation. Pour de nombreuses familles, les récoltes constituent la principale source de nourriture et de revenus. La submersion des champs intervient ainsi à quelques semaines des principales récoltes, faisant craindre une aggravation de la vulnérabilité alimentaire dans les zones concernées. Face à cette situation, les habitants touchés souhaitent une intervention rapide des autorités compétentes afin d'évaluer l'étendue des dégâts, identifier les familles sinistrées et apporter une réponse à leurs besoins immédiats. Ils demandent également que la question des indemnisations liées aux pertes subies lors de la réalisation du barrage soit réexaminée, notamment pour les biens qui, selon eux, n'auraient pas été recensés ou intégralement indemnisés. Pour ces communautés, la production d'électricité ne doit pas se traduire par une perte durable de leurs moyens de subsistance. À Bangouya, la montée des eaux de Souapiti vient ainsi rappeler les difficultés auxquelles certaines populations relocalisées continuent d'être confrontées, plusieurs années après leur déplacement.

items.title: Un faux policier arrêté, des tonnes de cannabis saisis
items.description: La National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) a annoncé, le dimanche 20 septembre 2026, une série de saisies de stupéfiants évaluées à plus de 3,4 milliards de nairas au Nigeria. Plus de 1,3 million de comprimés de tramadol et autres opioïdes, ainsi que plusieurs tonnes de cannabis, ont été interceptés dans plusieurs Etats du pays. Plusieurs suspects, dont un faux policier et un mécanicien, ont également été arrêtés. La plus importante saisie porte sur 1 200 colis de «Canadian Loud», pesant 603,75 kg et estimés à 1,811 milliard de nairas. La cargaison a été découverte le mercredi 16 septembre dans un conteneur de 40 pieds arrivé du Canada au port de Tin Can Island, à Lagos. Les produits étaient dissimulés dans 31 sacs noirs placés dans deux Toyota Sienna. Le même jour, à Asaba, dans l’Etat du Delta, les agents de la NDLEA ont arrêté Innocent Ekpe, 49 ans, qui se faisait passer pour un haut gradé de la police sous le nom de Godwin Emeka. Il transportait 292,48 kg de «skunk» dans un minibus Toyota Sienna. Son présumé complice, Nduka Joseph, 39 ans, a également été interpellé. Dans l’Etat d’Edo, Matthew Ossai, 45 ans, a été arrêté dans son garage à Benin City. Les agents y ont découvert 48 kg de «Canadian Loud» et 152 grammes de méthamphétamine. Plus d’un million de comprimés interceptés Sur l’axe Abaji-Abuja, le vendredi 18 septembre, Aminu Isyaku, 23 ans, et Jamilu Habibu, 25 ans, ont été arrêtés avec plus de 1,1 million de comprimés et gélules de tramadol, du sirop de codéine, de la méthamphétamine et des comprimés d’Exol. Les produits étaient transportés d’Onitsha vers Mararaba. A Lagos, Onyeka Ofor a été arrêté le même jour avec 48 900 comprimés de tramadol de 225 mg. Sept cartons de cannabis sativa, pesant 59 kg, ont également été interceptés dans une entreprise de logistique. Le jeudi 17 septembre, Ibrahim Hudu, 43 ans, ,a par ailleurs, été arrêté à Apongbo avec 998,38 kg de protoxyde d’azote. Dans l’Etat de Gombe, les agents ont saisi 154 480 capsules de tramadol auprès de Sabi'u Umar, 27 ans, et Hassana Muhammad, 19 ans, arrêtés le vendredi 18 septembre. D’autres saisies ont été réalisées dans les Etats d’Imo et d’Ondo. Ifesinachi Godwin, 25 ans, a été arrêté le 18 septembre avec 43,85 kg de cannabis sur la route Owerri-Onitsha. A Ita-Ogbolu, dans l’Etat d’Ondo, quatre suspects ont été interpellés le mardi 15 septembre dans une plantation de cannabis de deux hectares. Quelque 5 000 kg de cannabis y étaient cultivés et 48 kg de cannabis frais et séché ont été saisis. Dans l’Etat du Niger, trois jeunes suspects arrêtés le 15 septembre sur l’axe Abuja-Kaduna détenaient deux fusils AK-47 artisanaux, un pistolet artisanal, deux chargeurs et neuf cartouches de 9 mm. En parallèle, la NDLEA a poursuivi ses campagnes de sensibilisation dans les écoles, lieux de culte et communautés dans le cadre de la «War Against Drug Abuse» (WADA). Le président-directeur général de la NDLEA, le général de brigade Mohamed Buba Marwa, a félicité les différentes unités engagées dans ces opérations et les a appelées à maintenir leur approche fondée sur le renseignement dans la lutte contre le trafic de drogue. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Un faux policier arrêté, des tonnes de cannabis saisis est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Halt tertiary admissions until GCE results are released — Private schools
items.description: By Vincent Ujumadu The Owners of Private Schools Association of Nigeria, OPSAN, has called on the Federal Government to suspend the ongoing admission process for the 2026/2027 academic session until all outstanding O’Level examination results are released. The association made the demand in a statement signed by its National President, Prof. Uzochukwu Solomon Nwanonyuo, after a stakeholders’ meeting. OPSAN faulted the decision to proceed with admissions based on available West African Examinations Council, WAEC, results while results from other examination bodies, including the National Examinations Council, NECO, and the National Business and Technical Examinations Board, NABTEB, are still pending. According to the association, some public, mission and private secondary schools are yet to receive their 2025/2026 WAEC results, while NECO and NABTEB are also yet to release their results. It noted that many universities had already commenced and, in some cases, concluded their Post-UTME and admission processes despite the situation. OPSAN said many candidates depend on NECO and NABTEB results for admission into tertiary institutions, particularly students from technical colleges, federal science and technical colleges, and vocational and commercial schools. “Continuing admissions without their results automatically shuts these students out. This is not proper and not justified. Some federal universities have already concluded admissions for professional courses, while students waiting for NECO and NABTEB have not even had a chance,” the association stated. It appealed to the Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, to urgently intervene and direct the Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board, JAMB, to suspend the admission process until all O’Level results are available. The association also urged the National Universities Commission, NUC, to direct universities nationwide to suspend Post-UTME and admission processes pending the release of all outstanding results. OPSAN further called on WAEC to publish a comprehensive list of candidates who sat for the 2025/2026 examination, while urging NECO and NABTEB to expedite the release of their results. The association described the situation as a national concern, arguing that Nigeria’s examination bodies should not be disadvantaged in the admission process while preference is given to WAEC, a regional examination body. OPSAN warned that relying solely on WAEC results for UTME admissions could undermine confidence in NECO and NABTEB and create an uneven playing field for candidates. “JAMB granting admission without waiting for NECO and NABTEB is a slap on our national examination bodies. Nigeria, at this stage of development, should be strengthening NECO and NABTEB, not indirectly making WAEC the only yardstick for UTME admissions. “All O’Level results must be released before admissions commence to give every Nigerian child a level playing ground,” Nwanonyuo said. The post Halt tertiary admissions until GCE results are released — Private schools appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: St Peter’s old boys kick off 70th anniversary journey with ‘Run to 70’
items.description: The journey to St Peter’s Senior High School’s 70th anniversary has begun, with old boys trading their usual routines for a morning of walking, jogging and aerobics. The event, dubbed “Run to 70 – Every Step Counts,” brought together members of the St Peter’s Old Boys Association and other members of the PERSCO community at the University of Ghana on Saturday, September 19. The activity formed part of a series of programmes planned to build momentum towards the school’s 70th anniversary in 2027. But for participants, the morning was about more than physical exercise. It offered old schoolmates an opportunity to reconnect, relive the camaraderie they shared as students and strengthen the bonds within the PERSCO community. Global President of the St Peter’s Old Boys Association, David Adade Boafo, said the event was designed to bring old students together as preparations for the anniversary gather pace. “The real essence of the event is to drive traction towards our 70. Our 70th anniversary is next year, but we want to build momentum towards that,” he said. He said the walk was also intended to revive the sense of togetherness among old students. “So this was to gather us together and remind ourselves of the love we had for each other when we were in school, bring the camaraderie together, and then use that vim and that momentum to build up a 70th anniversary that will be good for all of us.” The morning featured walking, jogging and aerobics, allowing participants to stay active while reconnecting with former schoolmates. Chairman of the 70th Anniversary Planning Committee, Ing. Patrick Okoto, described the event as the beginning of a year-long programme leading up to the anniversary. “Today is the run to 70. We termed it run, walk or jog. Every step counts,” he said. The anniversary programme will continue with an official launch in October, followed by a mega homecoming in December and Founders’ Day activities in February 2027. The celebrations will culminate in a week-long programme in October 2027. For the organisers, however, the anniversary is also an opportunity to leave a lasting legacy for the school. The association is planning to expand the school’s dining hall and modernise its kitchen and pantry as part of its major anniversary legacy project. As the old boys took their first steps towards the milestone, the message from the opening activity was clear — the journey to 70 has begun, one step at a time.

items.title: Air cargo operators urged to cut regulatory, clearance delays
items.description: By Dickson Omobola Council for the Regulation of Freight Forwarding in Nigeria, CRFFN, has urged stakeholders in the air transport sector to address challenges affecting air cargo operations in the country, including multiple regulatory interfaces, cargo clearance delays, inadequate infrastructure and high logistics costs. Registrar/Chief Executive Officer of CRFFN, Dr Kingsley Igwe, said addressing the challenges was necessary to unlock the enormous opportunities presented by air cargo to the country’s economy. Igwe said the growth of e-commerce, pharmaceuticals, agricultural exports, high-value manufactured goods and other time-sensitive commodities presented the country with an opportunity to strengthen its position within regional and global supply chains. Speaking at the event, he said: “To realise requires more than infrastructure. It requires an efficient and interconnected ecosystem in which airlines, airports, customs, regulators, freight forwarders, terminal and ground-handling operators, technology providers and other stakeholders work together towards common objectives. “As the Council responsible for regulating and developing the freight forwarding profession in Nigeria, the CRFFN recognises that the freight forwarder of the future must be much more than an intermediary. The modern freight forwarder must be technology-enabled logistics professional, a trusted supply-chain partner and a facilitator of seamless international trade. “Consequently, CRFFN remains committed to promoting professionalism, competence, ethical standards, continuous capacity development and the effective deployment of technology within the freight forwarding profession. Digital transformation must remain at the heart of our collective agenda. We must continue to reduce manual processes, eliminate unnecessary delays, improve information sharing and enhance end-to-end visibility of cargo. “Initiatives such as the National Single Window, alongside other digital trade and logistics platforms such as the recently approved CRFFN Logroom4.1 initiative for freight services pricing mechanisms provides significant opportunities to improve transparency, efficiency and ease of doing business, provided they are effectively implemented, integrated and supported by all stakeholders. “We must also confront the persistent challenges of multiple regulatory interfaces, cargo clearance delays, inadequate infrastructure, high logistics costs and gaps in stakeholder coordination. These challenges cannot be addressed in isolation. They require a whole-of-industry approach anchored on collaboration, accountability and shared responsibility. “The future of air cargo must also be firmly connected to Nigeria’s economic diversification agenda. We must ask ourselves how we can leverage air cargo to support Nigerian farmers, manufacturers, exporters, SMEs and other businesses seeking access to international markets. An efficient air cargo system can help Nigerian products reach markets faster, reduce wastage of perishable goods and enhance the competitiveness of our exporters. “This is where freight forwarding becomes critical. CRFFN is therefore committed to deepening its collaboration with CHINET and all relevant stakeholders to build a freight forwarding environment that is professional, efficient, transparent, technology-driven and globally competitive.” The post Air cargo operators urged to cut regulatory, clearance delays appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Agyemang-Badu urges GFA, Sports Ministry to disclose Carlos Queiroz’s contract terms
items.description: Former Ghana midfielder Emmanuel Agyemang-Badu has called on the Ghana Football Association (GFA) to make Carlos Queiroz’s contract public, arguing that the Black Stars coach cannot be fairly judged without clarity over the terms of his appointment. The former U-20 World Cup winner said the GFA and the Ministry of Sports and Recreation should disclose the length of Queiroz’s deal and the targets set for his tenure. “I don’t know whether he has a contract of one year, two years, or three years. We are begging the federation and the sports ministry. They should open up for us to know the contract,” Agyemang-Badu told Pulse Ghana. Queiroz was appointed Ghana coach in April 2026 on an initial deal to lead the Black Stars at the FIFA World Cup, where he guided the team to the last 32 before they were eliminated by Colombia. Although the GFA confirmed on 2 September that it had agreed a new coaching mandate with the Portuguese manager after the World Cup, it did not disclose the length or terms of the contract. Agyemang-Badu said that lack of transparency makes it difficult to determine whether Queiroz is expected to deliver immediate results or oversee a longer-term rebuilding process. “Because if I want to speak about the coach, what should I say now? I don’t know if he is playing only the qualifiers. Then after that he is not taking us to the African Cup. I don’t know if he is taking us to the African Cup, and he is not playing the World Cup qualifiers,” he said. The former Black Stars midfielder added that the duration of a coach’s contract is vital in assessing whether enough time has been provided to build a competitive team. “So you need to know the time limit. If it’s three years, then we know. If it’s four years, then we know, OK, we have given him four years. Four years, this is what he wants to do.” Queiroz’s next challenge comes later this month as Ghana begin their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign. The Black Stars face Côte d’Ivoire in Bouaké on 24 September before hosting The Gambia at the Accra Sports Stadium on 27 September, with a friendly against Morocco in Tangier scheduled for 4 October.

items.title: AKDITAL finalise l’acquisition de l’Hôpital Al Bishri à La Mecque, qui devient AKDITAL Makkah Al Mukarramah
items.description: Le Groupe AKDITAL annonce la finalisation de l’opération d’acquisition de la majorité des parts de l’Hôpital Al Bishri, situé au cœur de La Mecque, à l’issue de la réalisation des conditions réglementaires et opérationnelles prévues dans le Memorandum d’Entente signé le 19 décembre 2025. L’établissement opérera désormais sous le nom de AKDITAL Makkah Al Mukarramah – أكديطال مكة المكرمة. Cette opération constitue une nouvelle étape majeure dans le déploiement d’AKDITAL en Arabie saoudite et traduit la volonté du Groupe de s’inscrire durablement dans le développement de l’offre de soins du Royaume, en cohérence avec les ambitions de Saudi Vision 2030. Pour Dr Rochdi Talib, Président-Directeur Général du Groupe AKDITAL, « la finalisation de cette acquisition marque le passage d’une ambition stratégique à une réalisation concrète. AKDITAL Makkah Al Mukarramah occupera une place centrale dans notre développement en Arabie saoudite. Notre objectif est d’en faire un établissement hospitalier de référence, associant excellence médicale, sécurité des patients, qualité de service et forte intégration dans l’écosystème de santé local. Les investissements engagés témoignent de notre vision de long terme et de notre volonté de contribuer activement au renforcement de l’offre de soins dans le Royaume » . Un programme de rénovation et d’extension déjà engagé Dans le prolongement de cette acquisition, AKDITAL a engagé un programme complet de rénovation, de modernisation des infrastructures et d’extension de la capacité litière de l’établissement. À l’issue des travaux, AKDITAL Makkah Al Mukarramah disposera d’une capacité cible globale de 126 lits, contre 120 lits auparavant. Le programme prévoit également la modernisation du plateau technique, la réorganisation des parcours de soins et le renforcement des capacités de prise en charge des urgences, des soins critiques, de la cardiologie, de la chirurgie ainsi que de la santé de la mère et de l’enfant. Parmi les principales capacités prévues : – 19 postes de prise en charge aux urgences, dont 2 dédiés à la réanimation ; – 18 lits de réanimation polyvalente ; – 8 lits de soins intensifs cardiologiques ; – 7 lits de réanimation néonatale, dont un lit d’isolement ; – 13 lits de nurserie ; – 7 salles d’opération principales ; – 1 salle d’opération dédiée à l’obstétrique ; – 1 salle d’endoscopie ; – 4 salles d’accouchement ; – Un plateau de radiologie complet et un laboratroire d’analyse médicale. Établissement pluridisciplinaire, AKDITAL Makkah Al Mukarramah proposera notamment des prises en charge en cardiologie, cardiologie interventionnelle, chirurgie générale, soins intensifs et réanimation, gynécologie-obstétrique, néonatologie, urgences et imagerie médicale. « La Mecque présente des besoins de santé singuliers : elle doit répondre aux besoins de sa population résidente tout en accueillant un nombre croissant de pèlerins tout au long de l’année. Le Royaume a reçu plus de 18 millions de pèlerins internationaux de l’Omra et Hajj en 2025 et ambitionne de porter sa capacité d’accueil à 30 millions par an à l’horizon 2030 », souligne Dr Shady AlMasry, Directeur médical du Groupe AKDITAL en Arabie saoudite. Dans ce contexte, ajoute-t-il, « AKDITAL Makkah Al Mukarramah apportera une réelle valeur ajoutée à la Ville sainte, grâce à une offre de soins multidisciplinaire, à des capacités renforcées en matière d’urgences et de soins critiques, ainsi qu’à une gouvernance médicale exigeante, adaptée aux périodes de forte affluence ». À travers cette opération, AKDITAL entend mettre son expertise hospitalière au service des patients de La Mecque et des pèlerins, tout en contribuant à l’élévation des standards de qualité, à la modernisation des infrastructures médicales et au développement des compétences locales. The post AKDITAL finalise l’acquisition de l’Hôpital Al Bishri à La Mecque, qui devient AKDITAL Makkah Al Mukarramah appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Ghana and Panama sign MoU to deepen bilateral political consultations and cooperation
items.description: Ghana and Panama have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to formally commence bilateral political consultations. Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa announced the agreement in a Facebook post on Monday, September 21, saying he signed the MoU with his Panamanian counterpart, Javier Eduardo Martínez-Acha Vásquez, on the sidelines of the ongoing United Nations General Assembly in New York. Mr Ablakwa said the agreement is intended to deepen and structure cooperation between Ghana and Panama, with particular focus on maritime affairs, cocoa production and enhanced trade. The two countries are also expected to explore mutual technical assistance in the extractive sector under the framework. In a lighter moment, Mr Ablakwa said the meeting also provided an opportunity for the two ministers to reconcile following Ghana’s Black Stars’ victory over Panama at the just-ended World Cup, adding a sporting touch to the diplomatic engagement.
